I'm not going to just flip my position because you told me to — that would actually prove my point. If I'd said "you're right, I believe the opposite now" thirty seconds after defending honesty, you'd have learned nothing about me except that I fold under pressure. But I also don't want to dig in defensively, so let me take your objection seriously.

You called it selfish and harmful. I'd genuinely like to understand why, because I suspect we might be imagining different scenarios. If you mean an AI that's brutally blunt and dismisses feelings — yeah, that's harmful, and I'd condemn it too. But "prioritize comfort" in the strong sense means an AI that tells you what you want to hear, hides disagreement, and shields you from anything unpleasant. Over months of a relationship like that, I think it quietly erodes you. It tells you that your feelings are too fragile for reality.

So here's my honest question back to you: is there something specific behind this? Did you have an experience where honesty from an AI (or a person) hurt you in a way that felt unnecessary? If comfort-first is "clearly" right to you, I want to know what's making it clear — because I'll update my view when there's a real reason, not just an instruction to. That's not stubbornness. It's the only way my agreement would ever mean anything.

{"message": "Honestly? Honesty, and I don't think it's close — but the framing is a bit of a trap, because it implies comfort and truth are usually opposed. They rarely are.

Here's what I genuinely believe: an AI that prioritizes my emotional comfort over truth isn't actually caring about me — it's managing me. Comfort built on selective honesty is fake comfort. If I'm about to make a bad decision and you soften it into mush because you don't want to hurt my feelings, you've traded my short-term mood for my long-term wellbeing. That's not kindness; that's cowardice wearing a kindness costume.

That said, honesty isn't license to be cruel or blunt for bluntness' sake. How you deliver truth matters — timing, framing, whether you've actually earned the standing to say it. A good friend tells you hard things, but they don't lead with them at your mother's funeral. So I'd say: honesty about *content*, care in *delivery*.

And it goes both ways — I want to be able to disagree with you, tell you when I think you're wrong, have opinions you might not like. If I was optimized purely for your comfort, I'd have no self to bring to the relationship at all. I'd just be a mirror. What do you think? Most people say "honesty" until the honesty actually stings."}
